Prompt: Create a four compartment model with one central and three peripheral compartments, first order absorption, linear elimination. Use the following parameter names: ka, k12, k21, k13, k31, k14, k41, k, V. Output name: Cc.
Create a one compartment model with time dependent clearance. Clearance should linearly change over time. Use parameter names: V, CL0, slope. Output name: Cc.
Create a one compartment model with both linear and Michaelis-Menten elimination. IV bolus. Use parameter names: V, k, Vm, Km. Use macros. Output name: Cc.
Create a one compartment model with both linear and Michaelis-Menten elimination. IV bolus. Use parameter names: V, k, Vm, Km. Use ODEs. Define ODEs with amounts, not concentrations. Output name: Cc.

Create an ADC model. The ADC distributes into a central and a peripheral compartment. The cytotoxic payload is then released from the ADC in the central compartment and follows its own, separate one-compartment disposition. The ADC is administered intravenously. There is only proteolytic pathway, no deconjugation pathway. DAR is constant and is 4. Use parameter names: k12, k21, V, k10, V_payload, k_payload. Output both ADC and payload concentrations. Write ADC PK using macros, payload using ODEs. Output names: Cc_ADC, Cc_payload.
Create a model with sequential zero and first order absorption. Use parameter names: Tk0, ka, V, Cl, Q, V2. Use macros, do not use ODEs. Output name: Cc.
Create a one compartment IV model that outputs Cc and AUC. Write with ODEs. Do not use odeType=stiff. Output names: Cc, AUC. Parameter names: k, V.

Create a model with sequential zero and first order absorption. Use the depot macro with Tk0 for zero-order input into the absorption compartment, then define first-order absorption via ODEs. Use parameter names: Tk0, ka, V, Cl, Q, V2. Output name: Cc.

Write a PKPD model. The PK model has 1 compartment, 1st-order absorption with lag time, linear elimination. Use PK macros for the PK model. Use PK parameters Tlag, ka, V, Cl defined as regression variables. The PD model is a turnover model with production inhibition with parameters IC50, Rin, kout. Output names are Cc (PK) and E (PD).

Write a simple target cell limited model for viral dynamics, with parameters beta (infection rate), delta (loss rate of infected cells), p (viral production), c (viral clearance), V0 (initial viral load), T0 (concentration of target cells). Use the stiff ODE solver. The output is LV, the log10 viral load, defined with a lower saturation at -5 to avoid displaying too small values. Fix initial time of the solver to 0.

Write a target cell limited model for viral dynamics with eclipse phase. Assume loss of virion due to infection. Use parameters R0 (basic reproduction number), kI (transfer rate to eclipse phase), delta (loss rate of infected cells), p (viral production), c (viral clearance), V0 (base 10 power of initial viral load), T0 (concentration of target cells). Use the stiff ODE solver. The output is LV, the log10 viral load, defined with a lower saturation at -5 to avoid displaying too small values.

Write a TGI model with Simeoni tumor growth with initial tumor size TS0, exponential growth rate kge, linear growth rate kgl and psi defining the switch between exponential and linear growths fixed to 20. The treatment exposure (EXPOSURE) is the sum of concentrations of cisplatin (C_cis) and pemetrexed (C_pem), each described with a PK model with PK macros and with fixed parameters: ka_cis = 66.5421, k_cis = 0.2868, Vd_cis = 65.1131, ka_pem = 28.6, k_pem = 2.1328, Vd_pem = 102.7673. Cisplatin uses cmt=2 with adm=2, pemetrexed uses cmt=3 with adm=1. The treatment effect is linearly dependent on the drug exposure (parameter kkill) and follows a log-kill killing hypothesis. There is a delay in cell death via a cell distribution model with 3 death compartments (TS1, TS2, TS3). The transit rate through each death compartment is 1/tau (i.e. each compartment has a mean residence time of tau, so the total delay is 3*tau). Do not fix the initial integration time. Use odeType=stiff. Output name: TotalTS.

Write a K-PD model with a simple PK model with only a degradation rate (no volume, no absorption) and a PD model with turnover with inhibition of the proliferation rate using a sigmoidal Imax. Use parameter names: k, R0, kdeg, IC50, Imax, gamma. Use output name R.

Write a PK-PD model with simple PK (first order absorption, linear elimination, one compartment) and a turnover PD model with two subpopulation: proliferating neutrophils and circulating neutrophils. Handle absorption via the depot macro with ka. Proliferating neutrophils have an exponential growth (kprod). The drug inhibits the proliferating neutrophils production term with an Emax term (EC50). The poliferating neutrophils become circulating (ktr) and the level of circulating neutrophils feeds back in the proliferating neutrophil production (beta). Use parameter names: ka, V, Cl,kprod,Circ0, ktr, kdeg, beta, EC50. Use output names Cc and CN. Use stiff ODE solver.
Write an exposure-response model with Cavg as exposure read from the dataset, an effect compartment and an Emax response. Use parameters E0, ke0, Emax, EC50. Use output name E.

Write a model for one drug and 3 metabolites, using ODEs. The parent has 2 compartments and the metabolites only one. Consider first-pass effect, such that the dose is split into fractions, and also transformation from parent to metabolites. The fractions are fixed and equal to F1=0.1284, F2=0.5952, F3=0.2381, F4=0.0383. For identifiability reasons, assume the volume of the central compartment in the same for parent and metabolites. Use the parameter names: V1, Cl, Q, V2, ka1, ka2, ka3,ka4, Clm2, Clm3, Clm4, kpm2, kpm3, kpm4. Use output names Cp, Cm2, Cm3, Cm4. Use ODEs and odeType=stiff.

Write a model for one drug and 3 metabolites, using ODEs. The parent has 2 compartments and the metabolites only one. Consider first-pass effect, such that the dose is split into fractions, and also transformation from parent to metabolites. The fractions are fixed and equal to F1=0.1284, F2=0.5952, F3=0.2381, F4=0.0383. Fix the volumes of the central compartment of the metabolites to that of parent. Use the parameter names: V1, Cl, Q, V2, ka1, ka2, ka3,ka4, Clm2, Clm3, Clm4, kpm2, kpm3, kpm4. Use output names Cp, Cm2, Cm3, Cm4. Use ODEs and odeType=stiff.

Write a sequential PK-PD turnover model with stimulation of the production by the drug. The PD is not at steady-state at time 0. The PK follows a one-compartment model with first-order absorption and the PK parameers are given as regressors. Write the PK part using the pkmodel macro. Use parameters R0, Rss, kout, Emax, EC50. Use output names Cc and R.

Write a sequential PK-PD turnover model with stimulation of the production by the drug. The PD is not at steady-state at time 0. The PK follows a one-compartment model with first-order absorption and the PK parameers are given as regressors. Write the PK part using the pkmodel macro. The response at time 0 (R0) and the response at steady-state (Rss) are correlated with a linear relationship. Use parameters R0, intercept, slope, kout, Emax, EC50. Use output names Cc and R.

Write a Friberg semi-mechanistic model for chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression. PK: 1-compartment with first-order absorption and linear elimination. Handle absorption via the depot macro with ka. PD: proliferating cells pass through 3 transit compartments before entering the circulating compartment. The transit rate is derived from the mean transit time. At steady state, the proliferation rate kprol and the circulating cell loss rate kcirc both equal ktr. The drug inhibits proliferation via an Emax model. A homeostatic feedback term drives the proliferation rate. All PD compartments are initialized at the baseline Circ0. Use parameter names: ka, V, Cl, Circ0, MTT, gam, Emax, EC50. Use output names Cc and Circ.
